title: Add drain command that lands via PR and rates the changed page
summary: Add an `athena drain` command that works the steward/audience queue itself within a user-set budget: run each item, land it through the `athena land --pr` path, then rate the live page. This retry fixes the rejected attempt's gap: a rating counts as "target met" only if taken after a landing. Audience is the repository owner, who now runs, lands and rates by hand.

defaults_applied.how: Fake-agent and stubbed-land tests for each stop reason and the land-before-rate ordering; clippy and fmt clean.
Criteria are checkable with cargo test, clippy, fmt and `drain --help`.
Fixes the missing land step instead of only documenting it, and guards the retry call with the budget.
README, CHANGELOG and decisions entries written for an outside reader.
The 'rated after landing' rule is enforced in code and pinned by tests, not by prose.
One command in a new module with minimal edits elsewhere.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The base has no drain command; the earlier attempt's changes were discarded, so this builds it whole, including the corrected land step.
Landing uses the same path as `athena land --pr` (Athena::land_pr / gh::land_pr), behind a trait or injected step so tests can stub it.

Stop reasons: target met, budget spent, repeated failure (same item failing twice), queue empty (not success). Items needing a person (above-ladder proposals) are listed as waiting and never accepted or landed.
'Target met' needs a rating taken after at least one landing in this run. If nothing landed, the output says the rating is of an unchanged page and does not report target met.
A budget check guards every model call, including the retry re-reading, not just job starts: spend plus the next call's cap must fit.
No new config key; the budget, rating threshold and job limit are CLI flags, recorded in docs/decisions.md.
tests/drain.rs is expected as a new file this time.

acceptance_criteria.text: `cargo test` passes, including fake-agent drain tests with a stubbed queue and stubbed land step that show: (1) each worked item is landed through the land step, (2) the rating is taken only after landing, (3) a pass that landed nothing cannot report 'target met' from a stale rating and the output says the page was unchanged.

Tests cover: two items landed then rating 4+ gives 'target met'; budget too small for the next call gives 'budget spent' with remaining items still queued; empty queue stops at once with no spend and says empty, not success; same item failing twice gives 'repeated failure' naming the item; a landing failure does not lead to a rating being taken as success.

A unit test pins that no job or model call (including the retry re-reading) starts when recorded spend plus its cap would exceed the budget, including when an earlier job's cost exceeded its estimate.
A test shows an above-ladder item needing a person is listed as waiting and left untouched, never accepted, approved or landed by the loop.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean; `cargo run -p athena-cli -- drain --help` documents the budget, rating-threshold and job-limit flags and lists the stop reasons.

The final output (text and --json) names the stop reason, jobs run with outcomes, costs and landing status, total spent, the latest rating against the target and whether it was taken after a landing, and the items still queued or waiting for a person.

README.md 'What it does not decide', CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md describe the command, that it lands through the PR path before rating, budget semantics, stop reasons, and the no-config-key decision; no text claims the owner must land by hand.

out_of_scope: Accepting, approving or landing above-ladder proposals that need a person.
Adding a config key for the budget or threshold.
Changing how the audience rating itself is produced.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
departures: Larger than the reference: the loop must be built from scratch with a stubbed land step and a git/PR-facing integration, and the prior attempt was rejected.
